answer: Continuous micro-fee decay. Each new identity pays a fee that doubles with the recent registration rate, so launching many identities in one window inflates the price sharply for every later one. An attacker’s cost curve rises superlinearly with fleet size, and each identity pays recurring per-transaction fees that only volume amortizes. A quiet voyage of registrations still leaves a costly plume in fees, and the decay rule gives every identity a lingering echo of that price.
